You can find out about the groups, events and networks (both in person and virtual) that are available to members of our staff community. Events on campus YorkConcerts A varied programme of guest performers and regular concerts by the University Symphony Orchestra, the 24 and the Chimera Ensemble. Open lectures Free lectures by expert speakers, aimed at a general audience. York Ideas Year-round events featuring talks by global speakers, family activities and learning experiences. Conferences and events York Conferences and Events hosts events including concerts, festivals, exhibitions and tribute acts on campus, with proceeds reinvested back into the University. Research events Events for staff and the general public including YorkTalks, Three Minute Thesis and Falling Walls Lab York. York Student Cinema YSC typically show three films per week during term time in P/X/001 (Exhibition Centre, Campus West). Screenings are open to staff and the public. Book a room on campus Events in York What's on in York York has a diverse mix of venues, showcasing music, art, cinema and comedy. YorkCard A YorkCard gives discounted entry to leisure facilities and attractions. Eventbrite Browse Eventbrite for events in York Sport and exercise Want to make new friends while achieving your fitness goals? Whether you want to try something new, join a team or drop in to a pay-as-you-go class, York Sport has a wide range of activities for you to choose from. Plus there are staff leagues in various sports, a weekly 5km parkrun, and fitness classes on campus. Sport at York Other activities The Languages Cafe Intercultural Peer Assisted Learning sessions, which provide a social space to practice conversation in eight languages University Choir Join the University Choir of 250 voices. They rehearse on Monday evenings during term and give concerts three times a year. Staff volunteering Volunteer during work time with York Cares to support a cause you care about. An award-winning community without limits Named Community University of the Year 2026. Our staff are the foundation of our success. We're proud to be The Mail University Guide’s Community University of the Year 2026. This award celebrates our York Festival of Ideas and our collective effort to create a positive environment for everyone. Whether you’re volunteering through York Cares or joining a staff network, you're part of a force for positive change. Read more about our award and impact Learn more about our vision: Our values and how we're working towards them How we're building a community without limits Join our staff networks and groups There are a number of social groups and networks for staff. Some coordinate in-person events and activities while others are informal online social communities within the University's Slack workspace. INCLUDE network , for colleagues with a disability or long-term health condition York Sustainability Network , for staff, students and alumni Women in Research Network A meeting of the Women in Research Network Family Network A group for anyone at the University with dependants. Men's Health @ York Get together, take part in activities and talk about physical and mental health. Rainbow Alliance This EDI staff network holds monthly socials including lunch clubs and pub meet-ups. Find more staff networks Join our Slack groups Veera posing by Central Hall, as featured on the #yorpaws Slack channel. Photo by Minna Lehtinen. Connect on Slack whether you are working on campus, or from home: Find peer support on #staff-autism-space , #rainbow-alliance If you're feeling creative, browse #artandcraft For nature appreciation try #yor-plants , #wildlifeofuoy Chat health and wellbeing on #staff-mental-health-wellbeing-networking , #menopause-staff-chat Animal lovers can head to #yorpaws , #catsofuoy Sustainability champions and bargain hunters convene on #recycle-chat , #recycle-for-sale-or-wanted Search for other groups or set up your own. Join the #slack-talk channel and look out for the monthly channel spotlights. Senior Common Rooms Members of staff can get involved in college life and access a vibrant social calendar by joining a Senior Common Room (SCR). Events can include illustrated talks, trips, cheese and wine evenings, book clubs, sports activities and quizzes. You'll also be invited to student-run events and can make use of the college's communal areas and amenities. Derwent College To find out more about joining Derwent SCR, contact derwent@york.ac.uk . Wentworth College All members of staff are welcome to join. Find out more by emailing wentworth-scrc@york.ac.uk . Ghana Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications Michigan State University Visiting Chefs exchange China Graduation University of Bergen CAS visit University of Munster University of Ghana Fudan University The Global Partnerships team works to develop strategic, multilayered partnerships with university and research partners across the world. We support and advise staff in their activities to grow a fruitful partnership. We offer region-specific expertise and provide advice about international partnerships, including how to develop and sustain research links at the individual, departmental and institutional level. Developing a formal partnership Whether you're involved in teaching or research, there's much to be gained from international collaboration. Broadly speaking there are three levels of collaboration or partnership. If you're interested in establishing a formal agreement with a partner institution or organisation, there are policies and procedures to follow. Please contact the Global Partnerships Team for support. York-Maastricht Partnership delegates A Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) can be considered as the formalisation of a partnership, which signals intent to explore and promote collaborative activities between two or more partners. While the agreement is not binding, it sets out the shared objectives for a partnership. University-level partnerships Our policy is to partner at this level with a small number of selected institutions which are recognised for their academic excellence and their commitment to internationalisation, where the ‘academic fit’ between us is complementary and relevant, and where the benefits of partnership are mutual. Developing an international teaching collaboration We support and advise on international partners and international regulation. The Academic Support Office sets up collaborative taught programmes , provides information on progression and articulation agreements , and offers policies and procedures. Funding opportunities The research contacts in your department are the first point of contact for identifying funding opportunities. Finding funding Research funding for international engagement Incoming and outgoing visits Visiting other institutions is an important part of building departmental and institutional links. We manage a programme of visits to countries which have been prioritised for the development of international links. We can facilitate visits to the University. If you would like to arrange a visit on behalf of an institution, get in touch at global-partnerships@york.ac.uk . Learn more about York Global Summer Schools Short courses for universities We offer year-round short courses and summer schools in York for groups of students or staff from universities around the world. If you'd like to develop a bespoke short course for your students or staff we'd welcome the opportunity to work with you and discuss your specific requirements. Our courses are designed to provide participants with an international experience in an increasingly globalised workplace, and encourage further student international mobility. Short courses for university students We've been running successful bespoke short courses for over 15 years. They last from one to 16 weeks and can include the following themes: A strong academic theme, such as History, Environmental Science etc. English language enhancement Intercultural awareness Employability and transferable skills Management and business skills Business English English language teacher development Academic and research skills Business, academic and cultural visits to places of interest Issues in culture and society Creativity Media and communication IELTS preparation Enquire about short courses Summer schools for university students Our summer schools are themed around an academic discipline. They involve lectures and seminars led by leading York academics in the arts and humanities, social sciences, and sciences and technology. Courses also include in-depth seminars, and practical participation by students, as well as visits to related places of interest for further study. Our teaching team provides academic skills support.
